questions.question: The language re-rank was found after your favorite idea failed the bar, on the same 201 photos — why report it as a shipped win rather than a lead needing a fresh held-out test?
questions.why: The speaker admits it was a post-hoc arm on the same test set, a classic forking-paths problem.

questions.question: Is the 'about 30 minutes a day' a timed measurement or your own estimate, and does it include the mornings spent reading results?
questions.why: The notes say it's his own count and explicitly excludes review time, understating the real human cost.

questions.question: Beyond the gate and flag, what stops an unattended agent run from merging broken code or overspending before you check on it?
questions.why: The idle-tab incident that burned a day's API allowance shows the guardrails were not airtight.

questions.question: The 65 percent right-card-in-top-3 figure on live lots comes from your own taps over five days — what's the sample size and confidence interval, and who else verified those calls?
questions.why: A single self-reported tapper is presented as ground truth for the headline live-accuracy number.

questions.question: The persona panel said the build was done and it was unusable on your phone the next morning — what makes you confident the redesigned panel process wouldn't fail the same way again?
questions.why: The gate itself was shown to produce a false pass, raising who reviews the reviewer.

questions.question: You showed four different ways of scoring top-3 accuracy that don't agree — why pick the roughly two-in-three number as the one headline claim instead of reporting a range?
questions.why: The backup slide admits the four yardsticks diverge, undercutting the single number used earlier in the talk.

questions.question: Is the forty-five-fork count and the claim that only two forks mattered a pre-registered tally, or a retrospective count made after you already knew which fixes worked?
questions.why: The notes concede the grid is his own count, not something in the record.

questions.question: Is the full experiment ledger and decisions log in the public repo, or are some of the sources you cited private?
questions.why: Nearly every claim cites internal files like decisions.md and arc notes whose public availability is unclear.

questions.question: When the usage limit cut off three build lanes mid-work, was any partially finished code merged before you caught it, or could that have happened?
questions.why: The notes mention lanes committing early specifically because of that cutoff, hinting at a near-miss.

questions.question: Your strongest model both writes the briefs and judges the results of the lanes it set up — what checks catch that model grading its own work favorably?
questions.why: Having one model author acceptance criteria and then judge against them is a reviewer-reviews-itself setup with no stated check.
